purpose: Identity, never a judgement about risk. Each entry records that a script body with this SHA-256 is the named script from the named published source, fetched on the recorded date. No entry says, or may be reworded to say, that a script is harmless: several of the scripts recorded here genuinely call eval() or exec(), and Blend X-Ray still reports that at full severity for every one of them. See the README section 'The known-good identity layer' for how to re-verify an entry and how to contribute one.
attestation: Every entry below was attested by one person, from files that person downloaded themselves. There is no second reviewer and no signature. Re-verify before relying on any of them.

entries.origin: CloudRig rig UI script, Blender Studio -- the copy embedded in the Sprite Fright open-movie shot 030_0020_A
entries.attested_by: Blend X-Ray maintainer (sole attester; not independently confirmed)
entries.notes: The user-interface script CloudRig writes into a .blend when it generates a rig. It draws the rig panel in the sidebar and provides the IK/FK snapping and keyframe baking operators animators use. It calls eval() twice, on the 'op_<property>' and 'prop_hierarchy' custom properties stored on a bone in the same file, to turn them back into the dicts that describe which buttons to draw; the strings it evaluates come from the .blend, so whoever edits the .blend chooses what gets evaluated. It also appends a handler to bpy.app.handlers.load_post and depsgraph_update_post. Neither callback carries the @persistent decorator, so Blender drops both the next time a file is loaded: BPY_python_reset calls BPY_app_handlers_reset(false), which keeps only callbacks tagged _bpy_persistent, and it does so before the incoming file's own scripts run. For as long as this file is the open one, the handler runs on every depsgraph update and every file load. This same body ships in at least nine published Blender Studio files, including Elder Sprite, Jay and the six Forest Animals rigs.

entries.origin: CloudRig rig UI script, Blender Studio -- the copy embedded in Rain v3.2
entries.attested_by: Blend X-Ray maintainer (sole attester; not independently confirmed)
entries.notes: The rewritten CloudRig rig UI script, found in the file named rain_v3.2.blend inside the Rain download archive. It is roughly 70 percent larger than the earlier revisions and, unlike them, parses the custom properties it reads with ast.literal_eval instead of eval, so Blend X-Ray's dynamic-code rule does not fire on it at all. Recorded here for identity, not because it is quieter.

entries.origin: Blender Studio character rigs (script by Sergey Sharybin)
entries.attested_by: Blend X-Ray maintainer (sole attester; not independently confirmed)
entries.notes: Binds hair particle systems to a proxy mesh so an armature can drive them indirectly, because hair particles cannot be rigged directly. It registers depsgraph_update_post and frame_change_post handlers. Neither is decorated @persistent, so Blender removes them when the next file is loaded; while this file is open they run on every depsgraph update and frame change. Ships in seven published Blender Studio files (Ellie, Jay, Phil, Victoria, and three of the Forest Animals rigs).

entries.origin: Blender Studio Sprite Fright shot pipeline (lib/scripts/load_settings.blend)
entries.attested_by: Blend X-Ray maintainer (sole attester; not independently confirmed)
entries.notes: Production shot-setup script. It looks for '<shot>.settings.json' and '<sequence>.settings.json' next to the .blend, opens them into text datablocks, and applies the values to objects whose names match. It parses those JSON files with eval() on the datablock contents rather than json.loads, which is why the dynamic-code rule fires; it also creates the settings file with open(path, 'a') when it is absent, which is why the file-write rule fires. Both settings files are empty in the published shot.

entries.origin: Blender Studio Sprite Fright shot pipeline (lib/scripts/load_settings.blend)
entries.attested_by: Blend X-Ray maintainer (sole attester; not independently confirmed)
entries.notes: Production lighting-override script. It applies per-shot lighting settings -- node values, motion-blur flags, per-object property overrides -- read from settings files next to the .blend. It builds assignment statements as strings and runs them with exec(), which is why the dynamic-code rule fires, and it opens settings files for append, which is why the file-write rule fires.

entries.origin: MD5 mesh/anim importer for Blender 2.41 by Bob Holcomb and Thomas 'der_ton' Hutter, embedded in the OpenGameArt rigged dwarf model
entries.attested_by: Blend X-Ray maintainer (sole attester; not independently confirmed)
entries.notes: A 2006-vintage id Software MD5 format importer, written against the Blender 2.4x Python API, carried inside the .blend as a text block. It reads .md5mesh and .md5anim files the user picks and builds meshes and armatures from them. It is Python 2 and cannot run on any current Blender, so none of Blend X-Ray's rules reach its body. Present in three published OpenGameArt downloads.

entries.origin: Generated by Blender's Rigify add-on -- reference body taken from the OpenGameArt 'Chickensoft chicken' rig
entries.attested_by: Blend X-Ray maintainer (sole attester; not independently confirmed)
entries.notes: The rig user-interface script Rigify writes into a .blend every time it generates a rig. It draws the rig sidebar panel and the IK/FK snapping, pole-toggle and bake operators. Line 10 assigns rig_id, a random per-rig identifier that Rigify appends to every operator and panel bl_idname so that two rigs in one scene do not collide -- which is exactly why this script's byte hash is different in every file that contains it and why it is recorded here by structure as well. It calls eval() once, on a bone-name list stored as a string in the rig's own data. This reference body is the one published in that OpenGameArt download; it is not a copy of Rigify's upstream template, and Rigify revisions other than this one will have a different structure.
